title: Per-layer QuantCompatibility Index and Amortized Dequant Routing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Add a lightweight per-layer QuantCompatibility Index (QCI) and an amortized dequant routing policy to reduce per-token dequant overhead while preserving mixed-precision accuracy. The goal is to pick kernel pipelines (INT8/FP8/FP16 hybrids) dynamically per-request and per-prefill window so we minimize cast/dequant ops for streaming decode workloads and stay within latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: QCI computed offline and available at model-load time for key transformer layers
Runtime selects kernel pipeline using QCI + request-level latency budget with <3% end-to-end token latency regression on 99th percentile compared to baseline mixed-precision path
Dequant runtime overhead (measured as extra microseconds per token) reduced by >= 35% on average for 512-token prefill windows on T4/A10G-like profiles
Canary rollout with automatic fallback to conservative mixed-precision path when telemetry indicates accuracy drop > 0.5% on eval prompts
tasks: Design QCI metric and offline microbenchmark harness (Ava)
Extend model loader to attach QCI per layer and store in model metadata (Diego)
Implement amortized routing policy in scheduler to group layers/ops by precision to avoid repeated casts (Eng-quant team)
Add zero-copy KV layout hint to minimize copies when switching precision (Infra)
Add telemetry for per-layer dequant cost, cast counts, and headwise variance (Observability)
Benchmark across representative models (gpt-like-1b/7b/13b) and hardware (T4, A10G, H100 sim)
Prepare canary plan and rollback criteria; coordinate with Console for rollout controls
comments: 2026-02-18 Ava Chen: Initial ticket created after perf retro. We saw repeated dequant overhead on streaming workloads where the same layer toggles precision per token. Proposal: compute a per-layer index that predicts net win for executing in lower precision vs paying dequant cost.

2026-02-23 Diego Morales: Prototype QCI formula: QCI = (kernel_speedup_ratio - dequant_cost_ratio) * stability_factor. Stability_factor derived from headwise variance and KV reuse score. Pushed a draft perf harness to https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/eng/quant-qci

2026-02-27 Performance notes: Offline microbench on 7B shows head layers (0..3) are small QCI wins for INT8 due to dequant setup; mid layers have strong QCI for INT8/FP8. Need to cap per-request switching to avoid thrashing.
2026-03-02 PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1832 contains QCI computation and model metadata plumbing. Requesting initial review from @mariam and @lee.

2026-03-05 Review feedback from Mariam: Add safety clamp so that QCI hysteresis window is at least two tokens; otherwise we get flip-flop with microbatch boundaries. Also ensure scheduler can override QCI for high-priority low-latency requests.

2026-03-07 Diego Morales: Implemented amortized routing in scheduler. Strategy: compute groupings across layers for the next prefill window and schedule kernels so that cast_count is minimized. Added tests to assert cast_count decrease on synthetic workload.

2026-03-10 Observability update: Added telemetry events quant.qci.value, quant.dequant_us, quant.cast_count, quant.kernel_choice per model/version. Dashboards draft: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/QCI-heatmap
decisions: Use a conservative default QCI threshold on hosted tier; aggressive threshold can be enabled per-customer via model config
Hysteresis of 2 tokens minimum to prevent precision flip-flop across microbatches
Zero-copy KV layout hint will be an opt-in flag at model-load to reduce risk in private deployments
Telemetry will control automatic rollback if eval prompt accuracy degrades > 0.5% over 1 hour
risks: Incorrect QCI calibration can cause accuracy regressions if layer sensitivity not detected
Scheduler grouping could increase tail latency for short requests if grouping window too large
Zero-copy changes may interact with on-prem memory layouts and require additional validation
